title: Criminal Law
audience: a law student in a U.S. JD program
purpose: Analyze the elements of crimes (act, mental state and causation), homicide, theft and property crimes, inchoate crimes, accomplice liability, and justification and excuse defenses, comparing the common law with the Model Penal Code.

weeks.1: The purposes of punishment and legality
weeks.3: Mental states under the common law and the Model Penal Code
weeks.4: Mistake of fact and mistake of law

blocks.deliverable: Decide whether five omissions can be criminal.
Assign the mental state required by each element of three statutes.
Classify five killings under the common law and the Model Penal Code.
Week 7 midterm; analyze a felony-murder problem.
Analyze attempt and conspiracy liability for three defendants.
Write an IRAC answer to a self-defense problem.
Submit the project; take an unseen 180 minute final in week 14.

project: Charging and defense memos: from a supplied police report, write a charging memo for the prosecutor and a defense memo on the strongest defenses, about 1,000 words each.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
